turns.question: Why did we switch sessions to JWT, and who did it?
turns.text:
Sessions were switched to JWT to relieve database load. The session table was the main source of DB load: issue #11 reported p95 DB CPU reaching 90% at login peaks with a hot sessions table [1]. PR #1, "feat(auth): switch sessions to JWT," replaced server-side sessions with short-lived JWTs, keeping refresh tokens server-side, and closes #11 [2][3]. The auth design doc records the same decision: 15-minute JWTs with server-side refresh tokens, decided in #1 after issue #11 [4].

It was authored by alice [2]. Issue #11 was filed by dave [1]. A later login redirect-loop fix (PR #6, by erin) addressed JWTs expiring mid-session [5].

turns.question: Why are invoice emails sometimes sent twice?
turns.text:
The graph points to a batch-job retry, but it does not confirm the root cause.

- Issue #14, "Invoice emails sometimes sent twice", is open. It was reported as seen twice in one month, with the note "may be the batch job retrying" [1].
- A comment on that issue says it is "Probably the batch retry from #4; needs an idempotency key" [2]. PR #4, "perf(billing): batch invoice generation", moved invoice generation to batches of 500 and is merged [3].
- Ticket PAY-6, "Invoice emails sent twice", is still in Todo and is linked to issue #14 [4].

So the likely explanation is that the batch-based invoice flow from PR #4 retries and re-sends emails, and the suggested fix is an idempotency key. The graph has no confirmed diagnosis or merged fix.
